author: Hodgson, 1831
summary: 우리나라에 드물게 찾아오는 길잃은새로, 겨울에는 숲 속 계류나 습지에서 홀로 지내는 일이 많다. 10월쯤 도착해 이듬해 4월 중순까지 머문다. 번식기에는 높은 산에 둥지를 짓고 알을 5개쯤 낳는다. 모족류, 복족류, 곤충 등을 주로 먹는다.

art.subject: Solitary Snipe (Gallinago solitaria), adult, as seen along Korean woodland streams in winter (October–April): crown blackish with a pale central stripe; face whitish with a dark eye-stripe and a dark cheek bar; upperparts dark brown with irregular rufous-brown and grey speckling and thin whitish lines along the mantle and scapulars; neck and upper breast warm brown with a little white mottling; lower breast and flanks white with dark brown bars; belly white; flight feathers plain brown; bill long and straight, greyish-olive at the base darkening towards the tip; dark eye; legs short, dull yellowish-green.
art.pose: standing alone at the edge of a forest stream, side view
art.scene: Korean winter woodland with a small stream and wet ground among the trees; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing at a stream edge: very long straight bill, whitish striped face, dark brown upperparts speckled rufous and grey with thin white mantle lines, plain brown flight feathers, brown neck and upper breast with a little white, dark-barred flanks, white belly, short greenish legs
adult, front view: brown upper breast lightly mottled white, dark brown bars on the lower breast and flanks, clean white centre to the belly
art.build: Large, bulky snipe, 30cm, clearly bigger and darker than Common Snipe; short neck, body held low and horizontal. Bill straight and very long, about twice the length of the head, often angled down while probing. Legs short, dull yellowish-green, with little bare tibia. Wings rounded; at rest the folded wings and tertials cover most of the short tail. When flushed it flies off heavily on broad wings that lack a white trailing edge.
avoid: Do not paint a white trailing edge to the wing or a warm buff face; those suit Common Snipe (Gallinago gallinago).
Do not curve the bill; it is long and straight.
Do not give it long legs or an upright stance; it crouches low on short legs.
Do not place it on open mudflat or reeds; it keeps to shaded, wet stream edges inside winter woodland.
